verified_scope: Original producer retains history and polling bytes before live broadcast and notification on local and exec-server paths.
History and polling each retain at most 1048576 bytes, half head and half tail; polling consumes only its own buffer.
The local producer consumes original stdout/stderr mpsc receivers and closes only after both streams close.
The live watcher registers close notification before Acquire state check, drains after completed output, and preserves a notification permit for a late exit watcher.
No new mutex order cycle was found; ordinary consumer reads the same producer history.
existing_limits: Ordinary polling retains its 50 ms post-exit wait cap; live watcher retains its 100 ms grace. terminate/Drop can still abort producer after observed exit.
Driver upstream broadcast Lagged handling is unchanged; the new regression deliberately saturates downstream only.
Exec-server recovery remains bounded by bytes retained by its original remote owner.
The two retained-byte buffer caps do not establish a whole-process memory cap.
